Put real photos of what you sell behind the headline, and keep one bright button as the only accent colour.

title: Full-bleed feast photo with two clear buttons
works: Full-width food photo fills the first screen
Big condensed headline is easy to read
Two buttons: order now or order catering
fixes: Phone headline overlaps a floating icon
Menu cards are cut off at the edge
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The first screen is one large photo of a holiday meal with a short headline on top. Two buttons sit under the line, one for ordering now and one for Thanksgiving catering. A visitor sees the food, reads the offer and picks a button within seconds.

## What works
- The photo fills the full width and shows real dishes, so the page feels warm and seasonal.
- The bold condensed headline stays readable over the photo on laptop and phone.
- The green and white buttons tell two kinds of visitor where to go.

## Where it is weak
- On the phone, an accessibility icon sits on top of the headline and hides some letters.
- The menu cards run off the right edge, and calorie numbers are the only detail shown on most.

## The lesson
Put a full-width photo of the real product behind a short headline, and give each type of visitor their own button.

title: Tall condensed type on deep green
works: Tall condensed headlines give a strong voice
Close portrait hero holds attention
Three short reasons sit right below hero
fixes: Risk warning pushes hero down the page
Hero text overlaps a busy photo on phone
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The page keeps to one deep green and one tall condensed type style, so it looks calm and serious for a risky product. A close portrait of a person fills the hero. The headline gives one claim with one button, and three short reasons follow below.

## What works
- The tall capital headlines are distinct and easy to read. They give the brand its own voice.
- A large face in the hero draws the eye and adds a human touch to a technical product.
- Three cards below the hero state the range, the safety and the features in a few words each.

## Where it is weak
- A grey risk warning sits above the hero and pushes the main message down the screen.
- On the phone the white hero text runs across a busy photo of people, and some words are hard to read.

## The lesson
Use one display typeface and one dark colour, and place a real face next to one clear claim and button.

title: Free-to-start promise over a lifestyle photo
works: Headline gives a clear free-to-start promise
Download button next to a second option
Review score and test badges build trust
fixes: Page feels like a standard security site
Phone hero text is dense over photo
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The page opens with a promise that costs the visitor nothing: free to start. A blue Download free button sits beside a lighter option for the paid plan. A review score and lab badges back up the claim straight away.

## What works
- The headline says free to start and only what you choose. The offer and the control are clear at once.
- Two buttons split the visitors into free and paid, so each has a path. The device list sits under them.
- A Trustpilot score sits in the hero, and independent test badges appear further down.

## Where it is weak
- The layout is polished but familiar: tabs, plan cards and wave edges. It does not stand out from other security brands.
- On the phone the headline and long subtext sit over a blurred photo and fill the screen.

## The lesson
Lead with the offer that removes cost risk, then put the proof beside the main button.

title: Tilted photo collage of real families
works: Tilted family photos feel warm and lively
Serif headings and peach colour feel gentle
Three numbers give proof in the hero
fixes: Three buttons in one block compete
Small text in the treatment cards
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The page shows the result a visitor hopes for: families with babies. The headline invites a first step, and the main button offers a free nurse consultation. Tilted photos on bright colour blocks make a sensitive topic feel warm and not clinical.

## What works
- The collage of parents and babies in tilted frames is the clear centre of the page. It is cheerful and human.
- Three figures sit under the headline: 33K babies born, 39 years of experience and 18 clinics. They give proof without long text.
- The main button offers something small and free, a nurse consultation. A hesitant visitor can say yes without commitment.

## Where it is weak
- A block of three buttons sits near the middle, with a list of links under it. The visitor must choose between many paths.
- The text in the treatment cards is small and light.

## The lesson
Offer one low-commitment first step as the main button, and show the happy result in the photos instead of the treatment.

title: Dusk cabin photo sells the escape itself
works: Moody dusk hero photo with a lit cabin
Search bar placed inside the hero
Cards list cabin traits with small icons
fixes: Cabin cards look like ordinary listings
Small body text on dark green sections
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The page sells a feeling, not a room. The hero photo shows a dark cabin with a warm lit window at dusk, and the headline lists what you give up: screens, scrolling and emails. The search bar sits in the same screen, so the visitor can act at once.

## What works
- The hero photo and the serif headline set a calm, quiet mood in one glance.
- The search bar with where, when and guests is part of the hero, so booking starts without scrolling.
- A green banner and a 4.8 rating from over 2,000 reviews sit under the hero as proof.

## Where it is weak
- The cabin cards follow a standard listing layout and look like many booking sites.
- Body text on the dark green sections is small and thin.

## The lesson
Lead with one photo that shows the feeling the customer wants, then put the booking tool right on it.

title: Green serif brand with painted home illustrations
works: Serif headline states the do-it-yourself saving
Rating and review count sit under the button
Painted dog and house give warmth
fixes: Pop-up covers the third feature card
Feature cards sit at uneven heights
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The headline tells the visitor they can do pest control themselves and save money. A single green button and a 4.7 rating with 30,000+ reviews sit right under it. The page feels friendly, not clinical.

## What works
- The serif headline in deep green is distinct from the usual pest control look. It states the benefit in two short lines.
- Three cards explain the plan, the application and the schedule, each with a photo and a short text.
- Soft illustrations of a dog and a house, in coral and pale blue panels, show the product is safe for pets and homes.

## Where it is weak
- A quiz pop-up sits over the third card on the laptop view, and a chat button covers the text on the phone.
- The three cards have different heights and offsets, which looks uneven.

## The lesson
Give a plain product its own type and colour, and put the rating right under the single main button.

title: Platform logos under a bold promise

The phone view keeps the headline and logos clean.

I'd make Get in touch more visible.
lessons:

Rise at Seven promise category leadership and show every search platform they cover.

## What works

- Rise at Seven show the platforms they cover, like Google, TikTok and Amazon, under the headline.
- Featured work names Sixt, Dojo and Magnet Trade in large type.
- The phone view keeps the headline and logos clean.

- I'd make Get in touch more visible.

Show the platforms you cover as logos under the headline.

title: Giant biscuit photo sells the free domain
works: Oversized biscuit photo makes the offer memorable
Headline and blue offer line read instantly
Domain search box sits right under the offer
fixes: Four hosting cards below look like a template
Badges under the search box add clutter
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The page opens with a two-line headline, "Nobody stops at just one," and a blue line that states the offer: buy a .uk domain, get one free. A large photo of two custard cream biscuits explains the idea at a glance. The search box sits right under the text, so the first action is also the first thing to do.

## What works
- The biscuit photo is unusual for a hosting company. It shows the "get two" idea without any extra words.
- The headline is big and dark, and the offer line is blue. The eye reads the joke first and the deal second.
- A single search field with one dark button is the only action in the first screen. The phone view keeps the same order, with the photo on top.

## Where it is weak
- Below the first screen, four hosting cards in a row look like any hosting site. The biscuit idea stops there.
- Four small certification badges sit under the search box. They add clutter next to the main action.

## The lesson
Pick one unexpected photo that explains your offer, and put the one action right next to it.

title: Phoenix mountain photo makes the page local
works: Headline names Phoenix and the driveway service
Sunset mountain photo shows the real place
Large 4.7 rating block with a review
fixes: Cash back offer text is long and tiny
Quote card is plain next to the dark hero
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
This is the Phoenix version of the Bang AutoGlass page. A black first screen has the headline "A Phoenix auto glass company that works in your driveway" and a photo of a white car parked in front of a red desert mountain. The red outline on the windshield and two buttons, a quote and a phone number, come next, followed by job count, rating and warranty.

## What works
- The headline names the city and the service, so a Phoenix visitor knows at once that the page is for them. The mountain in the photo backs this up.
- The page repeats the same type, red accent and car outline as the other Bang pages, so the local pages feel like one brand.
- Further down, a very large 4.7 rating sits over a dark car photo beside a customer review. The proof is easy to read.

## Where it is weak
- The Arizona cash back offer is in small text with several lines of conditions. It is hard to read, on the phone too.
- The quote card is a plain white box with small option tiles. It does not match the bold dark section above it.

## The lesson
For a local page, name the city in the headline and use a photo that could only be taken there.

title: Red panel with torn edge beside portrait
works: Heavy headline on solid red
Torn edge links text and portrait
Single dark Donate button is clear
fixes: Cookie bar takes space at the top
Phone hero cuts off the subline
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The hero is a solid red panel with a large bold headline and a torn edge that joins it to a calm portrait. One dark button says Donate now, so the next step is clear.

## What works
- The headline is heavy, short and easy to read on both screens.
- The torn paper edge gives a hand-made feel and ties the text to the photo.
- The dark Donate button stands out against the red panel.

## Where it is weak
- A dark cookie bar sits above the header and pushes the hero down.
- On the phone, the photo comes first and the supporting line is cut off before the button.

## The lesson
Put the headline on a solid brand colour, join it to a portrait with one distinctive edge, and keep one button.

title: Lime and coral blocks with outline headlines
works: Bold outline headlines give a party feel
Lime and coral blocks split the page
Google 5.0 rating and 35 years near the button
fixes: Hero photo is blurry and busy
Service tiles show no detail or next step
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The page looks like the events it sells. Big white and outline capitals, lime and coral colour blocks and photos of stage lighting give a lively tone from the first screen. A Google 5.0 rating and a lime Get In Touch button sit directly under the intro.

## What works
- The headline Event Creators and the line below it say what the company does in a few words.
- The first screen puts three proof points next to the button: 35 years, creativity and impact. A Google 5.0 rating sits above them.
- The second section tells the 1989 origin story and gives a figure: more than 5,000 events for a quarter of a million guests.

## Where it is weak
- The hero photo is a blurred crowd with coloured sticks, so it does not show a real event clearly.
- The service tiles show only a photo and a title, with no short line about what the client gets.

## The lesson
Let the page itself feel like the event, and place the rating and one hard figure beside the contact button.

title: Arched baby photo in warm terracotta
works: Arch-shaped photo feels warm and personal
Three proof numbers sit right by the headline
Insurance logos shown as a clear strip
fixes: Section headline is cut off on both sizes
Phone shows proof numbers clipped at the top
lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
Oula is a maternity practice, and the page feels like one. A mother and baby fill an arch-shaped photo, the colours are cream and terracotta, and the serif headline is calm. A Book now button and a phone number are always close.

## What works
- The arch-shaped photo of a mother and baby shows the outcome the buyer wants. It also gives the page a shape that is not a plain rectangle.
- Three numbers sit by the headline: babies delivered, insurance plans accepted and Google rating. They answer the first doubts without scrolling.
- A row of insurer logos follows the hero. A worried parent can check coverage at a glance.

## Where it is weak
- The terracotta headline block is cut off in the capture, so the text overlaps and is partly hidden.
- On the phone, the stats row is clipped at the top and the insurer logos are cut at the edge.

## The lesson
Put real portraits in a distinctive shape, and place proof numbers and insurance logos within the first two screens.

title: Booking form sits beside a moody photo
works: Dark photo and wine panel feel premium
Treatment, postcode and date fields in hero

- The "From ordinary to extraordinary" section sets "8x" and "3x" in huge type with a short line of text under each. The numbers stay in memory.

## Where it is weak
- The cookie banner shows twice on the laptop screens and covers the page text on the phone.
- The four-column promise section is small text with little to see, and it looks like many other sites.

## The lesson
Pick the two numbers that prove your product, set them very large with one line of text, and keep the consent banner from covering the page.

title: Giant headline over an orange e-bike close-up
works: Orange photo fills the whole first screen
White headline names the offer plainly
Model cards show monthly prices
fixes: Lower sections look like a plain template

lessons:
# Why this page wins leads
The first screen is a big orange photo of an e-bike handlebar, with a very large white headline: "Your full service E-Bike subscription". The colour and the type are bold, and the visitor knows the offer at once. A round white "Rent now" button sits under the text.

## What works
- The orange image has no clutter. It makes the page feel strong and modern, and it fits a bike brand.
- The three cards under "Our Offer" cover bikes, service and theft protection. They answer the main worries about a subscription.
- The model cards show a starting price per month, such as 149 euros, with two buttons each. A visitor can compare and start.

## Where it is weak
- After the hero, the page uses small grey text, plain white cards and the same bike picture again and again. It loses the bold feel.
- The hero button is small compared to the huge headline, and no price or proof appears in the first screen.

## The lesson
Use one strong colour photo and a very large plain headline for the first screen, then add a price or proof beside the button.

title: Warm coral waves make a sensitive topic friendly

Pelvic health is a private subject. This page uses warm coral, soft curves and a friendly rounded typeface so a visitor feels at ease. The first screen says what the service is, says it is covered by insurance, and gives one button: Schedule Visit.

- The icon row and card grid follow a common health-site pattern, so the lower page looks like a template.

For a private health topic, choose soft colour and curves, and answer the cost question in the first screen.
